messages:
anna_docs: Quick heads-up — the metering example under /docs/usage/metering.md (the Python "burst credits" snippet) can yield a negative remaining_quota when `used > allocation`. Repro steps in comments.

sam_engineering: ah good catch. The snippet does `remaining = allocation - used` without clamping. I hit this in load test when bursts overlap windows.

maria_prod: yikes — that's the kind of example customers copy verbatim. We should avoid implying negative quotas or negative billing :grimacing:

ben_sre: Agreed. Can we patch the snippet to be defensive and add a tiny unit test? Also flag the dashboard tooltip so it's consistent.

anna_docs: Plan: update code to `remaining = max(allocation - used, 0)` and add an inline comment about burst carryover semantics. I'll open a PR and link the dashboard copy change.

sam_engineering: sgtm. Also add a short note that meters are rolled up on an hourly window (so you can see transient spikes appear as higher hourly usage) — support has been getting this question.

anna_docs: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/582 — initial patch attached. CI says lint failing.

ci-bot: build failed — flake8 error in docs/snippets/metering.py: line 12 E501 line too long

anna_docs: fixing line wrap and will add a small unit test (pytests) for the clamp behaviour.

ben_sre: once lint/test pass can we merge and backport to release/v1.3? Support needs doc update shipped with today's release notes.

maria_prod: For the dashboard tooltip I'd like this copy: "Burst credits are applied when baseline pool consumption is exceeded; unused burst credits do not carry past the billing window." I'll paste into the PR comment.

anna_docs: added tooltip text and test. pinging @sam_engineering for variable-name nit.

sam_engineering: tiny nit: rename `allocation` -> `baseline_credits` to be clearer in the snippet. I'll push a 1-line commit to the PR.

ci-bot: build succeeded — all checks passed

anna_docs: Merged and cherry-picked to release/v1.3. Closing thread. :tada:
